---
title: "Local setup"
---

You can follow along in a [Codespace](setup-codespaces.qmd)
with nothing to install,
and the Codespace is where you can use GitHub Copilot for the homework.
To work on your own computer instead,
install everything below before Lecture 2.
None of it needs AI tools.

## A GitHub account

In Lecture 2 you'll make your own copy (a fork) of the course repository,
so you'll need a free GitHub account:
<https://github.com/signup>.

## R

Install R 4.5 or newer from CRAN:
<https://cloud.r-project.org/>.
Lecture 1 uses the `penguins` data built into R since version 4.5.

## An editor

Use either of these:

- Positron: <https://positron.posit.co/>
- RStudio Desktop: <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>

## Quarto 1.10 or newer

Install Quarto from <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>,
even if your editor came with its own copy.
The course website's theme needs Quarto 1.10 or newer,
and the copy that comes with Positron or RStudio is usually older.
With an older Quarto,
rendering stops with an error that says the "UBC brand" extension
"is incompatible with this quarto version".

After you install it,
restart your editor,
open its terminal,
and run:

```bash
quarto --version
```

It should print 1.10 or a higher number.

Quarto also makes the homework's PDF, using Typst,
so you don't need to install LaTeX.

## R packages

Run this once in the R console:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "tidymodels", "medicaldata", "knitr", "rmarkdown"
))
```

Quarto uses knitr and rmarkdown to run the R code in a document.

## Git

You'll clone your fork in Lecture 2.
Install Git by following *Happy Git and GitHub for the useR*:
<https://happygitwithr.com/install-git.html>.

## Check that it works

Once you've cloned your fork in Lecture 2,
open `example.qmd` and render it,
as the [Clone the repository](lecture-02/01-clone-the-repo.qmd) page shows.
If it renders, everything you need is installed.
If you use RStudio,
also follow that page's tip on running chunks from the top folder.
